statement: While a Quest step is pending, the pending step's pin is the single base source for every attempt recorded against it: a one-shot solve attempt, continue --summary and the autonomous loop all record the pinned base instead of re-pinning fresh HEAD (scripts/solve/pending-step.js owns the decision table pending pin -> epoch base -> HEAD, typed ATTEMPT_BASE_SOURCE), so attempts of one step never disagree on base and the review envelope's candidate fingerprint always composes; solve correct-attempt-base is widened to repair an attempt whose base drifted from a sibling accepted attempt's recorded base as well as from a candidate rejection, only when the recorded delta is byte-identical at both bases (typed refusal otherwise). No refusal of commits while a step is pending is introduced. Proven deterministically on the real Solver modules with the exact operator sequence of 2026-08-30 (begin step, unrelated commit advancing HEAD, one-shot attempt, mint review): red on HEAD (mixed bases, unlandable), green after.

constraints.statement: If this Quest changes source code, spawn a subagent verifier before audit and git handoff, then record a Solver finding with evidence subagent:<id>.
The Solver landing/attempt owner under scripts/solve remains the single authority; no duplicated predicate is introduced elsewhere.

The pending step's pin is the single base source for every attempt recorded while it is pending (one-shot attempt, continue, and the autonomous loop alike); no attempt path re-derives a base from HEAD while a step is pending.

A base correction is admitted only by the standing candidate rejection or a sibling accepted attempt's recorded base, and only when the delta is byte-identical at both bases; otherwise it fails closed with a typed reason.
No new refusal of commits while a step is pending is introduced; later attempts keep their recorded base when HEAD advances, as canon requires.
Proof is a deterministic replay of the recorded operator sequence through the real Solver modules on a temporary repository fixture, red on HEAD and green after, with controls that must stay green.
